target_name: Total Net Capital Return by Knowledge-Rich Firms
rationale: Internally consistent and directionally coherent, but it is a one-leg broadening of the archive's already-tested winner (equity payout → net total external financing, i.e., the well-known net-external-financing anomaly) and therefore closer to a cosmetic variant than a new mechanism.

The commitment-versus-opportunism contrast against the archived buyback leg is a legitimate and cleanly specified discrimination test, though dvc/at is largely a profitability/quality proxy, so the result risks reducing to the known R&D × profitability interaction and the zero-dividend mass will pile ties at the bottom of the second rank.

A reasonable coverage-driven repair of the archived fading-productivity signal, but the second leg is mechanically induced by the first — issuance inflates `at` and thus depresses ΔR&D/at — so the interaction may be little more than a nonlinear restatement of the composite-issuance anomaly, compounded by ΔR&D=0 for all non-R&D firms.

The two legs are mechanically entangled (high lt/at implies small ceq, which inflates R&D-stock/ceq), and the ceq denominator inverts the signal exactly for the negative- or near-zero-book-equity R&D firms the hypothesis targets, so the construct does not measure the intended intangible-adjusted leverage distortion.

This is a rediscovery of the archived "Funding Instability of Intangible-Dependent Firms" with the expected sign flipped post hoc to match its realized alpha and a gross→net financing tweak, i.e., a data-fitted story rather than an independent hypothesis, and its cross-sectional evidence was already flat (t = -0.22).

target_name: Innovation Peak During Own Financing Drought
rationale: Within-firm time-series percentile positioning is a genuinely different state concept from the archive's cross-sectional interactions, though the rank difference is additive rather than conditional, a 5-observation TS_RANK is coarse, and zero-R&D firms yield degenerate ties that will contaminate the long leg.
